findings: SSC 2026 recommends an initial MAP target of 65 mmHg over higher targets (strong, moderate certainty), managed as a range (for example within 5 mmHg), and suggests an initial MAP range of 60–65 mmHg for adults aged 65 years or older (conditional, low certainty).

findings: ALPS (NEJM 2016): neither drug significantly improved survival to discharge overall; a possible benefit was seen in bystander-witnessed arrests.

trials.name: ANDROMEDA-SHOCK
findings: ANDROMEDA-SHOCK found a non-significant trend to lower mortality with capillary refill-targeted resuscitation, with less organ dysfunction at 72 hours.
trials.title: Effect of a resuscitation strategy targeting peripheral perfusion status vs serum lactate levels on 28-day mortality among patients with septic shock: the ANDROMEDA-SHOCK randomized clinical trial
trials.reference: Hernández G, Ospina-Tascón GA, Damiani LP, et al. Effect of a resuscitation strategy targeting peripheral perfusion status vs serum lactate levels on 28-day mortality among patients with septic shock: the ANDROMEDA-SHOCK randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2019;321(7):654–664.

trials.name: APEC
findings: ERCP is probably indicated for persistent biliary obstruction, but routine urgent ERCP in predicted severe gallstone pancreatitis without cholangitis did not improve outcomes (APEC trial).

trials.name: APROCCHSS
findings: APROCCHSS (hydrocortisone 50 mg every 6 hours plus fludrocortisone 50 µg) showed lower 90-day mortality (43% vs 49.1%).
trials.title: Hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone for adults with septic shock
trials.reference: Annane D, Renault A, Brun-Buisson C, et al. Hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone for adults with septic shock. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(9):809–818.

trials.name: ARMA
findings: ARMA randomised 861 patients and showed lower mortality (31.0% vs 39.8%) with 6 mL/kg PBW and plateau pressure ≤30 cmH2O, compared with 12 mL/kg PBW and plateau ≤50 cmH2O.

trials.name: ARREST
findings: Routine gentamicin increases nephrotoxicity without benefit, and adjunctive rifampicin did not improve outcomes in the ARREST trial.

trials.name: ART
findings: ART randomised 1010 patients to stepwise recruitment manoeuvres (up to 60 cmH2O) with decremental PEEP titration, or low PEEP.
trials.title: Effect of lung recruitment and titrated positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) vs low PEEP on mortality in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome: a randomized clinical trial
trials.reference: Writing Group for the Alveolar Recruitment for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Trial (ART) Investigators. Effect of lung recruitment and titrated positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) vs low PEEP on mortality in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2017;318(14):1335–1345.

trials.name: ATHOS-3
findings: ATHOS-3 showed that angiotensin II improved MAP response at 3 hours (69.9% vs 23.4%) and allowed reduction of catecholamine doses, but it was not powered for mortality.
trials.title: Angiotensin II for the treatment of vasodilatory shock
trials.reference: Khanna A, English SW, Wang XS, et al. Angiotensin II for the treatment of vasodilatory shock. N Engl J Med. 2017;377(5):419–430.

trials.name: BICAR-ICU
findings: SSC 2021 suggests against bicarbonate for hypoperfusion-induced lactic acidaemia in general, but suggests it for patients with pH ≤7.2 and AKIN stage 2 or 3, based on BICAR-ICU, which showed lower mortality and less need for renal replacement therapy in that subgroup.
trials.title: Sodium bicarbonate therapy for patients with severe metabolic acidaemia in the intensive care unit (BICAR-ICU): a multicentre, open-label, randomised controlled, phase 3 trial
trials.reference: Jaber S, Paugam C, Futier E, et al. Sodium bicarbonate therapy for patients with severe metabolic acidaemia in the intensive care unit (BICAR-ICU): a multicentre, open-label, randomised controlled, phase 3 trial. Lancet. 2018;392(10141):31–40.

trials.name: BLING III
findings: BLING III showed a non-significant reduction in 90-day mortality, with meta-analyses favouring continuous infusion.
trials.title: Continuous vs intermittent β-lactam antibiotic infusions in critically ill patients with sepsis: the BLING III randomized clinical trial
trials.reference: Dulhunty JM, Brett SJ, De Waele JJ, et al. Continuous vs intermittent β-lactam antibiotic infusions in critically ill patients with sepsis: the BLING III randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2024;332(8):629–637.

trials.name: BRAIN-ICU
findings: BRAIN-ICU found that one in four survivors had cognitive impairment at 12 months comparable to mild Alzheimer disease, and longer delirium duration was independently associated with worse cognition.
trials.title: Long-term cognitive impairment after critical illness
trials.reference: Pandharipande PP, Girard TD, Jackson JC, et al. Long-term cognitive impairment after critical illness. N Engl J Med. 2013;369(14):1306–1316.

trials.name: CANONIC
findings: The CANONIC study defined ACLF as acute decompensation of cirrhosis with organ failure (liver, kidney, brain, coagulation, circulation, respiration) and 28-day mortality above 15%.

trials.name: CAPE COD
findings: CAPE COD randomised 800 ICU patients with severe CAP (excluding septic shock and influenza) to hydrocortisone 200 mg/day for 4–8 days with taper, or placebo.
trials.title: Hydrocortisone in severe community-acquired pneumonia
trials.reference: Dequin PF, Meziani F, Quenot JP, et al. Hydrocortisone in severe community-acquired pneumonia. N Engl J Med. 2023;388(21):1931–1941.

trials.name: CLASSIC
findings: CLASSIC randomised 1554 patients with septic shock who had received at least 1 L of fluid.
trials.title: Restriction of intravenous fluid in ICU patients with septic shock
trials.reference: Meyhoff TS, Hjortrup PB, Wetterslev J, et al. Restriction of intravenous fluid in ICU patients with septic shock. N Engl J Med. 2022;386(26):2459–2470.

trials.name: COACT
findings: Randomised trials (COACT, TOMAHAWK) found no survival benefit from routine immediate angiography in resuscitated patients without ST elevation.
trials.title: Coronary angiography after cardiac arrest without ST-segment elevation
trials.reference: Lemkes JS, Janssens GN, van der Hoeven NW, et al. Coronary angiography after cardiac arrest without ST-segment elevation. N Engl J Med. 2019;380(15):1397–1407.

trials.name: CONFIRM
findings: CONFIRM showed verified HRS reversal in 32% with terlipressin vs 17% with placebo, but serious respiratory failure was more common (14% vs 5%), related to fluid overload and severe ACLF.

trials.name: CRASH-3
findings: CRASH-3 randomised over 12,000 TBI patients.

trials.name: CULPRIT-SHOCK
findings: CULPRIT-SHOCK showed lower 30-day death or renal replacement therapy with culprit-only PCI compared with immediate multivessel PCI.
trials.title: PCI strategies in patients with acute myocardial infarction and cardiogenic shock
trials.reference: Thiele H, Akin I, Sandri M, et al. PCI strategies in patients with acute myocardial infarction and cardiogenic shock. N Engl J Med. 2017;377(25):2419–2432.

trials.name: DECRA
findings: DECRA enrolled patients with diffuse TBI and ICP above 20 mmHg for 15 minutes despite first-tier therapy.
trials.title: Decompressive craniectomy in diffuse traumatic brain injury
trials.reference: Cooper DJ, Rosenfeld JV, Murray L, et al. Decompressive craniectomy in diffuse traumatic brain injury. N Engl J Med. 2011;364(16):1493–1502.

trials.name: DEVICE
findings: DEVICE randomised 1417 patients and found higher first-attempt intubation success with video laryngoscopy (85.1% vs 70.8%), with no difference in severe complications.
Video laryngoscopy is now commonly recommended as a first-line device in critically ill patients.
trials.title: Video versus direct laryngoscopy for tracheal intubation of critically ill adults
trials.reference: Prekker ME, Driver BE, Trent SA, et al. Video versus direct laryngoscopy for tracheal intubation of critically ill adults. N Engl J Med. 2023;389(5):418–429.

trials.name: DEXA-ARDS
findings: Both the 2024 ATS ARDS update and SCCM corticosteroid update suggest corticosteroids for ARDS, based on trials such as DEXA-ARDS (dexamethasone 20 mg/day for 5 days then 10 mg/day for 5 days), which reduced mortality and increased ventilator-free days.
trials.title: Dexamethasone treatment for the acute respiratory distress syndrome: a multicentre, randomised controlled trial
trials.reference: Villar J, Ferrando C, Martínez D, et al. Dexamethasone treatment for the acute respiratory distress syndrome: a multicentre, randomised controlled trial. Lancet Respir Med. 2020;8(3):267–276.

trials.name: ECLS-SHOCK
findings: ECLS-SHOCK randomised 420 patients and found no mortality benefit from routine ECLS, with increased moderate or severe bleeding and peripheral vascular complications.
trials.title: Extracorporeal life support in infarct-related cardiogenic shock
trials.reference: Thiele H, Zeymer U, Akin I, et al. Extracorporeal life support in infarct-related cardiogenic shock. N Engl J Med. 2023;389(14):1286–1297.

trials.name: EOLIA
findings: EOLIA included PaO2/FiO2 <50 mmHg for over 3 hours, PaO2/FiO2 <80 mmHg for over 6 hours, or pH <7.25 with PaCO2 ≥60 mmHg for over 6 hours despite optimisation.
trials.title: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for severe acute respiratory distress syndrome
trials.reference: Combes A, Hajage D, Capellier G, et al. Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for severe acute respiratory distress syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(21):1965–1975.

trials.name: EPaNIC
findings: EPaNIC randomised 4640 patients; withholding PN until day 8 led to fewer infections, shorter ICU stay, fewer ventilator days and lower healthcare costs.
trials.title: Early versus late parenteral nutrition in critically ill adults
trials.reference: Casaer MP, Mesotten D, Hermans G, et al. Early versus late parenteral nutrition in critically ill adults. N Engl J Med. 2011;365(6):506–517.

trials.name: EPVent-2
findings: EPVent-2 randomised 200 patients and found no difference in the composite of death and days free from mechanical ventilation between oesophageal pressure-guided PEEP and an empirical high PEEP–FiO2 strategy.
trials.title: Effect of titrating positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) with an esophageal pressure-guided strategy vs an empirical high PEEP-FiO2 strategy on death and days free from mechanical ventilation among patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome: a randomized clinical trial
trials.reference: Beitler JR, Sarge T, Banner-Goodspeed VM, et al. Effect of titrating positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) with an esophageal pressure-guided strategy vs an empirical high PEEP-FiO2 strategy on death and days free from mechanical ventilation among patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2019;321(9):846–857.

trials.name: ESETT
findings: ESETT randomised patients with benzodiazepine-refractory status epilepticus to levetiracetam 60 mg/kg, fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg or valproate 40 mg/kg; seizure cessation and improved responsiveness occurred in about 45–47% with each, with similar adverse events.
trials.title: Randomized trial of three anticonvulsant medications for status epilepticus
trials.reference: Kapur J, Elm J, Chamberlain JM, et al. Randomized trial of three anticonvulsant medications for status epilepticus. N Engl J Med. 2019;381(22):2103–2113.

trials.name: FACTT
findings: FACTT compared conservative and liberal fluid strategies after shock resolution.
trials.title: Comparison of two fluid-management strategies in acute lung injury
trials.reference: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) Clinical Trials Network. Comparison of two fluid-management strategies in acute lung injury. N Engl J Med. 2006;354(24):2564–2575.

trials.name: FLORALI
findings: FLORALI randomised 310 patients; intubation rates did not differ overall, but 90-day mortality was lower with HFNO, and intubation was reduced in the subgroup with PaO2/FiO2 ≤200 mmHg.
trials.title: High-flow oxygen through nasal cannula in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure
trials.reference: Frat JP, Thille AW, Mercat A, et al. High-flow oxygen through nasal cannula in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure. N Engl J Med. 2015;372(23):2185–2196.

trials.name: HALT-IT
findings: HALT-IT randomised 12,009 patients and found no reduction in death due to bleeding, while venous thromboembolic events and seizures were more frequent.

trials.name: HIGH-WEAN
findings: HIGH-WEAN showed that alternating prophylactic NIV with HFNO reduced reintubation within 7 days compared with HFNO alone (11.8% vs 18.2%), especially in hypercapnic patients.
trials.title: Effect of postextubation high-flow nasal oxygen with noninvasive ventilation vs high-flow nasal oxygen alone on reintubation among patients at high risk of extubation failure: a randomized clinical trial
trials.reference: Thille AW, Muller G, Gacouin A, et al. Effect of postextubation high-flow nasal oxygen with noninvasive ventilation vs high-flow nasal oxygen alone on reintubation among patients at high risk of extubation failure: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2019;322(15):1465–1475.

trials.name: HOT-ICU
findings: HOT-ICU randomised 2928 patients and found no difference in 90-day mortality or serious adverse events between lower (PaO2 60 mmHg) and higher (90 mmHg) targets.
trials.title: Lower or higher oxygenation targets for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure
trials.reference: Schjørring OL, Klitgaard TL, Perner A, et al. Lower or higher oxygenation targets for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure. N Engl J Med. 2021;384(14):1301–1311.

trials.name: IABP-SHOCK II
findings: IABP-SHOCK II randomised 600 patients and found no difference in 30-day (or long-term) mortality.
trials.title: Intraaortic balloon support for myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock
trials.reference: Thiele H, Zeymer U, Neumann FJ, et al. Intraaortic balloon support for myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock. N Engl J Med. 2012;367(14):1287–1296.

trials.name: IMPRESSION
findings: Opioids delay gastric emptying and reduce early platelet inhibition by oral P2Y12 inhibitors (IMPRESSION trial).

trials.name: INTUBE
findings: INTUBE found major adverse peri-intubation events in about 45% of patients, with cardiovascular instability the most common (about 43%), followed by severe hypoxaemia (9%) and cardiac arrest (3%).
trials.title: Intubation practices and adverse peri-intubation events in critically ill patients from 29 countries
trials.reference: Russotto V, Myatra SN, Laffey JG, et al. Intubation practices and adverse peri-intubation events in critically ill patients from 29 countries. JAMA. 2021;325(12):1164–1172.

trials.name: LOVIT
findings: LOVIT randomised 872 ICU patients with sepsis on vasopressors and found a higher composite of death or persistent organ dysfunction at 28 days with vitamin C.
trials.title: Intravenous vitamin C in adults with sepsis in the intensive care unit
trials.reference: Lamontagne F, Masse MH, Menard J, et al. Intravenous vitamin C in adults with sepsis in the intensive care unit. N Engl J Med. 2022;386(25):2387–2398.

trials.name: MERINO
findings: The MERINO trial showed higher mortality with piperacillin–tazobactam compared with meropenem for ceftriaxone-resistant E. coli or Klebsiella bacteraemia.

trials.name: MIND-USA
findings: MIND-USA also found no effect of haloperidol or ziprasidone on delirium duration.
trials.title: Haloperidol and ziprasidone for treatment of delirium in critical illness
trials.reference: Girard TD, Exline MC, Carson SS, et al. Haloperidol and ziprasidone for treatment of delirium in critical illness. N Engl J Med. 2018;379(26):2506–2516.

trials.name: MINT
findings: MINT randomised 3504 patients with MI and haemoglobin below 10 g/dL.
trials.title: Restrictive or liberal transfusion strategy in myocardial infarction and anemia
trials.reference: Carson JL, Brooks MM, Hébert PC, et al. Restrictive or liberal transfusion strategy in myocardial infarction and anemia. N Engl J Med. 2023;389(26):2446–2456.

trials.name: MIST2
findings: MIST2 showed that combined intrapleural tPA and DNase improved radiographic pleural opacity and reduced surgical referral and hospital stay, whereas either agent alone was ineffective.
trials.title: Intrapleural use of tissue plasminogen activator and DNase in pleural infection
trials.reference: Rahman NM, Maskell NA, West A, et al. Intrapleural use of tissue plasminogen activator and DNase in pleural infection. N Engl J Med. 2011;365(6):518–526.

trials.name: NICE-SUGAR
findings: Intensive insulin therapy (NICE-SUGAR) increased mortality and hypoglycaemia in critically ill patients.
NICE-SUGAR showed higher mortality and severe hypoglycaemia with intensive targets of 4.5–6 mmol/L.
trials.title: Intensive versus conventional glucose control in critically ill patients
trials.reference: NICE-SUGAR Study Investigators; Finfer S, Chittock DR, Su SY, et al. Intensive versus conventional glucose control in critically ill patients. N Engl J Med. 2009;360(13):1283–1297.

trials.name: NUTRIREA-2
findings: NUTRIREA-2 found no difference in 28-day mortality or ICU infections between enteral and parenteral early nutrition at full calories in shock, but enteral feeding was associated with more vomiting, diarrhoea, bowel ischaemia and acute colonic pseudo-obstruction.
trials.title: Enteral versus parenteral early nutrition in ventilated adults with shock: a randomised, controlled, multicentre, open-label, parallel-group study (NUTRIREA-2)
trials.reference: Reignier J, Boisramé-Helms J, Brisard L, et al. Enteral versus parenteral early nutrition in ventilated adults with shock: a randomised, controlled, multicentre, open-label, parallel-group study (NUTRIREA-2). Lancet. 2018;391(10116):133–143.

trials.name: OptimaCC
findings: OptimaCC was stopped early because adrenaline was associated with higher incidence of refractory cardiogenic shock, higher heart rate and lactate, despite similar effects on cardiac index and MAP.
trials.title: Epinephrine versus norepinephrine for cardiogenic shock after acute myocardial infarction
trials.reference: Levy B, Clere-Jehl R, Legras A, et al. Epinephrine versus norepinephrine for cardiogenic shock after acute myocardial infarction. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2018;72(2):173–182.

trials.name: OSCILLATE
findings: OSCILLATE was stopped early because of higher in-hospital mortality with HFOV (47% vs 35%), associated with more sedation, neuromuscular blockade and vasoactive use.
trials.title: High-frequency oscillation in early acute respiratory distress syndrome
trials.reference: Ferguson ND, Cook DJ, Guyatt GH, et al. High-frequency oscillation in early acute respiratory distress syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2013;368(9):795–805.

trials.name: PANTER
findings: The PANTER trial showed that a step-up approach (percutaneous drainage followed, if needed, by minimally invasive necrosectomy) reduced major complications and death compared with primary open necrosectomy.
trials.title: A step-up approach or open necrosectomy for necrotizing pancreatitis
trials.reference: van Santvoort HC, Besselink MG, Bakker OJ, et al. A step-up approach or open necrosectomy for necrotizing pancreatitis. N Engl J Med. 2010;362(16):1491–1502.

trials.name: PARAMEDIC2
findings: PARAMEDIC2 randomised OHCA patients to adrenaline or placebo; adrenaline increased ROSC and 30-day survival, but the difference in survival with favourable neurological outcome was not significant, and more survivors on adrenaline had severe neurological impairment.
trials.title: A randomized trial of epinephrine in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
trials.reference: Perkins GD, Ji C, Deakin CD, et al. A randomized trial of epinephrine in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. N Engl J Med. 2018;379(8):711–721.

trials.name: PATCH
findings: PATCH showed that platelet transfusion increased death or dependence at 3 months in antiplatelet-associated ICH not needing surgery.
trials.title: Platelet transfusion versus standard care after acute stroke due to spontaneous cerebral haemorrhage associated with antiplatelet therapy (PATCH): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial
trials.reference: Baharoglu MI, Cordonnier C, Al-Shahi Salman R, et al. Platelet transfusion versus standard care after acute stroke due to spontaneous cerebral haemorrhage associated with antiplatelet therapy (PATCH): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial. Lancet. 2016;387(10038):2605–2613.

trials.name: PEITHO
findings: PEITHO showed that tenecteplase reduced the combined outcome of death or haemodynamic decompensation within 7 days, mainly through less decompensation, but increased major extracranial bleeding and haemorrhagic stroke (2% vs 0.2%).
trials.title: Fibrinolysis for patients with intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism
trials.reference: Meyer G, Vicaut E, Danays T, et al. Fibrinolysis for patients with intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism. N Engl J Med. 2014;370(15):1402–1411.

trials.name: PREOXI
findings: PREOXI randomised 1301 patients and found that pre-oxygenation with NIV reduced hypoxaemia (SpO2 below 85%) during intubation from 18.5% to 9.1%, without increasing aspiration.
trials.title: Noninvasive ventilation for preoxygenation during emergency intubation
trials.reference: Gibbs KW, Semler MW, Driver BE, et al. Noninvasive ventilation for preoxygenation during emergency intubation. N Engl J Med. 2024;390(23):2165–2177.

trials.name: PRESERVE
findings: PRESERVE randomised 5177 patients and found no benefit of bicarbonate over saline, or of acetylcysteine over placebo, for preventing adverse renal outcomes after angiography.
trials.title: Outcomes after angiography with sodium bicarbonate and acetylcysteine
trials.reference: Weisbord SD, Gallagher M, Jneid H, et al. Outcomes after angiography with sodium bicarbonate and acetylcysteine. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(7):603–614.

trials.name: PROPPR
findings: PROPPR randomised 680 trauma patients; mortality was not significantly different overall, but the 1:1:1 group had more haemostasis and fewer early exsanguination deaths, without increased complications.
trials.title: Transfusion of plasma, platelets, and red blood cells in a 1:1:1 vs a 1:1:2 ratio and mortality in patients with severe trauma: the PROPPR randomized clinical trial
trials.reference: Holcomb JB, Tilley BC, Baraniuk S, et al. Transfusion of plasma, platelets, and red blood cells in a 1:1:1 vs a 1:1:2 ratio and mortality in patients with severe trauma: the PROPPR randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2015;313(5):471–482.

trials.name: PROSEVA
findings: PROSEVA enrolled patients with severe ARDS (PaO2/FiO2 <150 mmHg, FiO2 ≥0.6, PEEP ≥5) after a 12–24-hour stabilisation period.
PROSEVA used a mean duration of 17 hours per session; meta-analyses show benefit when proning lasts more than 12 hours per day in moderate-to-severe ARDS.
In PROSEVA, cardiac arrest rates were not increased; meticulous turning procedures and padding reduce complications.
trials.title: Prone positioning in severe acute respiratory distress syndrome
trials.reference: Guérin C, Reignier J, Richard JC, et al. Prone positioning in severe acute respiratory distress syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2013;368(23):2159–2168.

trials.name: REDOXS
findings: REDOXS found a trend towards higher 28-day and significantly higher 6-month and in-hospital mortality with high-dose glutamine, especially in patients with renal dysfunction.
trials.title: A randomized trial of glutamine and antioxidants in critically ill patients
trials.reference: Heyland D, Muscedere J, Wischmeyer PE, et al. A randomized trial of glutamine and antioxidants in critically ill patients. N Engl J Med. 2013;368(16):1489–1497.

trials.name: REDUCE
findings: GOLD recommends prednisolone 40 mg daily for 5 days; the REDUCE trial showed 5 days was non-inferior to 14 days for re-exacerbation, with lower steroid exposure.
REDUCE trial: 5 days of prednisone was non-inferior to 14 days.
trials.title: Short-term vs conventional glucocorticoid therapy in acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: the REDUCE randomized clinical trial
trials.reference: Leuppi JD, Schuetz P, Bingisser R, et al. Short-term vs conventional glucocorticoid therapy in acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: the REDUCE randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2013;309(21):2223–2231.

trials.name: RENAL
findings: The RENAL and ATN trials showed no benefit of higher-intensity CRRT (40 vs 25 mL/kg/h).
trials.title: Intensity of continuous renal-replacement therapy in critically ill patients
trials.reference: RENAL Replacement Therapy Study Investigators. Intensity of continuous renal-replacement therapy in critically ill patients. N Engl J Med. 2009;361(17):1627–1638.

trials.name: RESCUEicp
findings: RESCUEicp randomised patients with refractory intracranial hypertension (above 25 mmHg) to craniectomy or continued medical care including barbiturates.
trials.title: Trial of decompressive craniectomy for traumatic intracranial hypertension
trials.reference: Hutchinson PJ, Kolias AG, Timofeev IS, et al. Trial of decompressive craniectomy for traumatic intracranial hypertension. N Engl J Med. 2016;375(12):1119–1130.

trials.name: REST
findings: REST randomised 412 patients and was stopped early for futility; ECCO2R did not reduce 90-day mortality and was associated with more serious adverse events, including intracranial haemorrhage and bleeding.
trials.title: Effect of lower tidal volume ventilation facilitated by extracorporeal carbon dioxide removal vs standard care ventilation on 90-day mortality in patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure: the REST randomized clinical trial
trials.reference: McNamee JJ, Gillies MA, Barrett NA, et al. Effect of lower tidal volume ventilation facilitated by extracorporeal carbon dioxide removal vs standard care ventilation on 90-day mortality in patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure: the REST randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2021;326(11):1013–1023.

trials.name: REVISE
findings: REVISE randomised 4821 ventilated patients; pantoprazole reduced clinically important upper GI bleeding (1.0% vs 3.5%) without significant differences in 90-day mortality, ventilator-associated pneumonia or C. difficile infection.
trials.title: Stress ulcer prophylaxis during invasive mechanical ventilation
trials.reference: Cook D, Deane A, Lauzier F, et al. Stress ulcer prophylaxis during invasive mechanical ventilation. N Engl J Med. 2024;391(1):9–20.

trials.name: ROSE
findings: ROSE (2019) compared early cisatracurium with a lighter-sedation strategy and stopped for futility, with no mortality difference.
The ATS 2024 guideline makes a conditional recommendation for neuromuscular blockers in early severe ARDS, reflecting heterogeneous evidence (ACURASYS benefit; ROSE no benefit).
trials.title: Early neuromuscular blockade in the acute respiratory distress syndrome
trials.reference: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute PETAL Clinical Trials Network. Early neuromuscular blockade in the acute respiratory distress syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2019;380(21):1997–2008.

trials.name: SAFE
findings: SAFE showed no overall mortality difference between albumin and saline.
trials.title: A comparison of albumin and saline for fluid resuscitation in the intensive care unit
trials.reference: Finfer S, Bellomo R, Boyce N, et al. A comparison of albumin and saline for fluid resuscitation in the intensive care unit. N Engl J Med. 2004;350(22):2247–2256.

trials.name: SEDCOM
findings: SEDCOM showed dexmedetomidine reduced delirium compared with midazolam.
trials.title: Dexmedetomidine vs midazolam for sedation of critically ill patients: a randomized trial
trials.reference: Riker RR, Shehabi Y, Bokesch PM, et al. Dexmedetomidine vs midazolam for sedation of critically ill patients: a randomized trial. JAMA. 2009;301(5):489–499.

trials.name: SMART
findings: SMART randomised over 15,000 adults and showed a lower composite of death, new renal replacement therapy or persistent renal dysfunction (14.3% vs 15.4%) with balanced crystalloids.
Secondary analyses of SMART and SALT-ED, and small trials, suggest faster resolution of DKA with balanced crystalloids, partly by avoiding hyperchloraemic acidosis.
trials.title: Balanced crystalloids versus saline in critically ill adults
trials.reference: Semler MW, Self WH, Wanderer JP, et al. Balanced crystalloids versus saline in critically ill adults. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(9):829–839.

trials.name: SPICE III
findings: SPICE III randomised 4000 patients; early dexmedetomidine did not reduce 90-day mortality, and most patients still required supplemental propofol or midazolam to achieve light sedation.
trials.title: Early sedation with dexmedetomidine in critically ill patients
trials.reference: Shehabi Y, Howe BD, Bellomo R, et al. Early sedation with dexmedetomidine in critically ill patients. N Engl J Med. 2019;380(26):2506–2517.

trials.name: STARRT-AKI
findings: STARRT-AKI found no survival benefit from accelerated RRT initiation and more RRT dependence at 90 days.
STARRT-AKI randomised 3019 critically ill patients with severe AKI.
trials.title: Timing of initiation of renal-replacement therapy in acute kidney injury
trials.reference: STARRT-AKI Investigators. Timing of initiation of renal-replacement therapy in acute kidney injury. N Engl J Med. 2020;383(3):240–251.

trials.name: STOP-IT
findings: In the STOP-IT trial, about 4 days of antibiotics after source control in intra-abdominal infection was as effective as longer courses.

trials.name: STOPAH
findings: STOPAH showed a non-significant short-term mortality reduction with prednisolone and no benefit of pentoxifylline.
trials.title: Prednisolone or pentoxifylline for alcoholic hepatitis
trials.reference: Thursz MR, Richardson P, Allison M, et al. Prednisolone or pentoxifylline for alcoholic hepatitis. N Engl J Med. 2015;372(17):1619–1628.

trials.name: SUP-ICU
findings: SUP-ICU found no mortality difference with pantoprazole but fewer clinically important bleeding events.
trials.title: Pantoprazole in patients at risk for gastrointestinal bleeding in the ICU
trials.reference: Krag M, Marker S, Perner A, et al. Pantoprazole in patients at risk for gastrointestinal bleeding in the ICU. N Engl J Med. 2018;379(23):2199–2208.

trials.name: TOMAHAWK
findings: Randomised trials (COACT, TOMAHAWK) found no survival benefit from routine immediate angiography in resuscitated patients without ST elevation.
trials.title: Angiography after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest without ST-segment elevation
trials.reference: Desch S, Freund A, Akin I, et al. Angiography after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest without ST-segment elevation. N Engl J Med. 2021;385(27):2544–2553.

trials.name: TracMan
findings: TracMan randomised 909 patients and found no difference in 30-day mortality between early and late tracheostomy.
trials.title: Effect of early vs late tracheostomy placement on survival in patients receiving mechanical ventilation: the TracMan randomized trial
trials.reference: Young D, Harrison DA, Cuthbertson BH, Rowan K; TracMan Collaborators. Effect of early vs late tracheostomy placement on survival in patients receiving mechanical ventilation: the TracMan randomized trial. JAMA. 2013;309(20):2121–2129.

trials.name: TRICC
findings: TRICC supported restrictive thresholds in general ICU patients.
TRICC found similar 30-day mortality with restrictive and liberal strategies, with lower mortality in younger and less severely ill patients receiving restrictive transfusion.
trials.title: A multicenter, randomized, controlled clinical trial of transfusion requirements in critical care
trials.reference: Hébert PC, Wells G, Blajchman MA, et al. A multicenter, randomized, controlled clinical trial of transfusion requirements in critical care. N Engl J Med. 1999;340(6):409–417.

trials.name: TRISS
findings: TRISS showed similar 90-day mortality and fewer transfusions with a threshold of 7 g/dL versus 9 g/dL in septic shock.
trials.title: Lower versus higher hemoglobin threshold for transfusion in septic shock
trials.reference: Holst LB, Haase N, Wetterslev J, et al. Lower versus higher hemoglobin threshold for transfusion in septic shock. N Engl J Med. 2014;371(15):1381–1391.

trials.name: TTM2
findings: TTM2 found no difference in mortality or functional outcome between targeted hypothermia at 33 °C and normothermia with early treatment of fever.
trials.title: Hypothermia versus normothermia after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
trials.reference: Dankiewicz J, Cronberg T, Lilja G, et al. Hypothermia versus normothermia after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. N Engl J Med. 2021;384(24):2283–2294.

trials.name: VASST
findings: VASST showed no mortality difference overall, but vasopressin spares catecholamines.
trials.title: Vasopressin versus norepinephrine infusion in patients with septic shock
trials.reference: Russell JA, Walley KR, Singer J, et al. Vasopressin versus norepinephrine infusion in patients with septic shock. N Engl J Med. 2008;358(9):877–887.

trials.name: WATERFALL
findings: WATERFALL was stopped early because aggressive fluid (20 mL/kg bolus then 3 mL/kg/h) increased fluid overload (20.5% vs 6.3%) without reducing moderately severe or severe pancreatitis.
trials.title: Aggressive or moderate fluid resuscitation in acute pancreatitis
trials.reference: de-Madaria E, Buxbaum JL, Maisonneuve P, et al. Aggressive or moderate fluid resuscitation in acute pancreatitis. N Engl J Med. 2022;387(11):989–1000.

trials.name: WOMAN
findings: FIGO recommends uterine massage, oxytocin as first-line uterotonic and tranexamic acid 1 g IV within 3 hours of birth (repeat if bleeding continues after 30 minutes), based on the WOMAN trial, which showed reduced death from bleeding.
WOMAN (Lancet 2017): TXA 1 g IV (second dose if bleeding continues after 30 min) reduced death due to bleeding, particularly when given within 3 hours, without increasing thromboembolism.

sofaNote: SOFA-2 note: a revised score, SOFA-2 (JAMA 2025), keeps six organ systems (renamed brain, respiratory, cardiovascular, liver, kidney and hemostasis), updates the organ-support drugs and devices used for scoring, revises several thresholds and adds alternative variables when measurements are unavailable; it predicted ICU mortality slightly better (AUROC 0.79 vs 0.77). Sepsis-3 is defined with the original SOFA score, so this calculation uses the original SOFA.
